mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (GDPC1) below its 12-month moving average signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when GDPC1 is below its 12-month moving average, or if the correlation between GDPC1 and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market stress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5%, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO is above its 6-month moving average, or if the correlation between INDPRO and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and consumer confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST is increasing, or if the correlation between HOUST and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases, or if the joint correlation between these labor market indicators and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with a rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases and CPIAUCSL increases, or if the joint correlation between these monetary indicators and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, or if the correlation between RSAFS and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
